text.p: Iraq's Minister of Labour and Social Affairs Latif Nsayyif Jassem has been removed from the post so he can devote his time to work for the ruling Baath party, according to a decree by President Saddam Hussein reported by the official Iraqi News Agency (INA) on Tuesday.
Jassem was replaced by Abdul-Hamid Aziz Mohammed Saleh, INA said, quoting a second decree. Further information about the new minister was not immediately available.

"Latif Nsayyif Jassem is relieved from the post of minister of labour and social affairs...in order to devote his time to work for the (ruling) Arab Baath Socialist party," said INA, quoting one of the two presidential decrees.
The official al-Qadissiya newspaper said on Tuesday that the decision of removing Jassem from his post was taken at a meeting of the regional command of the party chaired by Saddam on Monday.
Jassem, a former information minister, was elected in October senior member to the party's regional command, the highest authority in Iraq after the ruling Revolutionary Command Council.
"The party's literature states that the main task of the elected member is to dedicate his time for party work," one of the decrees said.
The paper said the meeting also decided to dismiss any Baath party member involved in usury and said strict punitive measures will be taken against such money lenders.
